summary: The candidate meets the request and passes all eight criteria. It adds docs/design/jev-code-health.md, entry D131 (marked proposed) in docs/decisions.md, and a CHANGELOG.md entry, and nothing else changed. The new design builds on the existing Jev client, fake, live test and score-jev scorer, and every path and name it cites matches the code: I checked them with ls and grep. Each of the five build jobs is marked reuse, extend or new, and none rebuilds a client, fake or scorer. Batching cites jev.rs request_body. The price range $0.000012 to about $0.00002 per call matches defaults-loop.md lines 259 and 667, and call counts and costs are labeled estimates. Each of the five questions gives its state, options, criteria, a numeric threshold and an effect. The doc also defines the shadow period, the exit rule, the evidence labels, how they feed labeled.rs, and how the design fits with 5p65 (marked assumed), Hestia and the scope guard. Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` passed. I found one minor issue: the exit rule's fallback to a person deciding sits awkwardly beside "never judged by a person" in the evidence section. There is also one nit about labeling J3.
